html:
The Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes are a union of three peoples of western Montana: the Bitterroot Salish, the Pend d'Oreille and the Kootenai. The map shows their homelands in 1492, in the valleys and mountains west of the Continental Divide.

The Bitterroot Salish and the Pend d'Oreille spoke Salishan languages. The Kootenai, or Ktunaxa, spoke a language unrelated to any other. They fished, gathered camas and bitterroot, and crossed the mountains to hunt bison on the plains once they had horses.

In 1805 the Salish met the Lewis and Clark Expedition and gave it horses. In 1855 the Hellgate Treaty with the United States set aside the Flathead Reservation around Flathead Lake, and the three peoples were grouped there as one confederation. The Bitterroot Salish were forced out of their own valley onto the reservation in 1891. The tribes still govern the reservation today.
